site.name: Dīvān-i Shahr-i Iṣfahān — Civic Register of the City of Isfahan
site.concept: The public civic register and bureau of records for the royal city of Isfahan, serving the residents of the Naqsh-e Jahan quarters.

card_pattern: Cards are square-ish modules sitting on an ivory field, each crowned by a slim ogee-arch silhouette in cobalt with a thin gold filet at its springing line. Inside, a centered display heading in Marcellus sits above generously leaded EB Garamond body text; a small turquoise palmette closes the card. Borders are 1px gold with a 6px cobalt inner rule, and corner medallions are stamped from the Islamic-star seal.
design_rules: The site holds a strict central axis on every page: ornament concentrates at borders, spandrels, and section heads while body fields breathe in cream. The cobalt–turquoise–gold–ivory axis is enforced; oxblood appears only for emphasis and seals. Geometric tessellation lives on borders and dividers; arabesque palmettes accent inline ornament — the two never overlap in the same band.

pages.title: Dīvān-i Shahr — Civic Register of Isfahan
pages.content_brief: Public-facing entry hall for the Civic Register. A tall iwan-style hero declares the bureau's name and the year (1108 A.H. / 1697 C.E.), with a centered proclamation from the Mayor of the Quarters, Mīrzā Ḥusayn Khān Shīrāzī. Beneath, three medallion modules announce the day's notices: water-allotment schedule for the Madi Niāsarm canal, the caravan-tax filing window, and the mourning observance for the late chief of the cloth-bazaar.

pages.title: Edicts & Public Notices — Dīvān-i Shahr
pages.content_brief: A chronological register of edicts (farmān) and bazaar proclamations issued from the office of the muḥtasib. Entries dated by the Hijri calendar, beginning 14 Rabīʿ al-Awwal 1108, list ordinances on bread weights, public-fountain repair in the Jūbāra quarter, and a prohibition on grazing within the Maydān-i Naqsh-e Jahān. Each notice carries the seal-mark of the issuing officer.

pages.title: Petitions & Public Audience — Dīvān-i Shahr
pages.content_brief: Procedure and schedule for citizens wishing to lodge petitions (ʿarīḍa) before the city secretariat. Audience is held in the columned veranda of the Bureau on the mornings of Saturday and Tuesday; petitioners must present themselves with two witnesses and the appropriate stamped paper from the chancery. The page enumerates fees, drafting conventions, and the order of precedence by guild and quarter.

pages.title: The Bureau & Its Officers — Dīvān-i Shahr
pages.content_brief: Account of the founding of the Civic Register under Shāh ʿAbbās the Great in 1006 A.H., with the present roster of officers: the Mayor Mīrzā Ḥusayn Khān, the Inspector of Markets Āqā Ṣādiq Tabrīzī, the Master of Waters Ustād Ibrāhīm of Yazd, and the Chief Scribe Mīr Muḥammad-Bāqir. Closes with the bureau's charge: the keeping of true records, the just measure of bread, and the proper repair of canals and bridges.

pages.title: Quarters, Canals & Bazaars — Dīvān-i Shahr
pages.content_brief: Civic directory of the twelve administrative quarters of Isfahan, the four principal canals (Madi Fadan, Madi Niāsarm, Madi Farshādī, Madi Tīrān) and their water-wardens, and the thirty-eight registered bazaar guilds with their elders. Names, addresses near recognized landmarks (the Qaysariyya Gate, the Chahār Bāgh, the Khwājū Bridge), and audience days are tabulated in two parallel columns.

pages.title: Visit the Dīvān — Hours & Direction
pages.content_brief: Practical guidance for visitors. The Bureau sits on the western arcade of the Maydān-i Naqsh-e Jahān, three doors north of the Qaysariyya Gate; chancery hours are from the second hour after dawn to the call for ẓuhr prayer, Saturday through Wednesday. Includes notes on appropriate dress, the resting bench in the courtyard for elderly petitioners, and the location of the public scribes opposite the entrance.
